text:
ops-bot: Pager: geo-dns anomaly detected - elevated NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL rates from eu-west resolvers for api.redwood.com. Severity: P2. On-call: @Leah. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/dns/geo-dns-eu
Leah: seeing spikes in SERVFAIL from multiple edge probes ~3m ago. Queries to Cloudflare EU resolvers returning SERVFAILs then succeeding on retry.
Diego: my probe set also shows a regional pattern - eu-west-1 and eu-west-2. Route53 looks fine from control plane side. Could be resolver flap or packet loss.
Rina: I'm in the EU on-call channel too; customers reporting intermittent 500s when hitting inference endpoints. Correlating with DNS errors.
Leah: starting narrow mitigation: add static fallback A for the eu geo-set pointing at eu-central origin, and lower TTL to 20s. Will coordinate with Tom for Route53 change.
Tom: ready. Two-step plan: 1) upsert fallback record with set identifier eu-west-fallback -> eu-central IP, TTL 20. 2) change routing policy health to prefer fallback while we investigate.
Leah: executing step 1.
Leah: Command sent:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z9REDWOOD --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-fallback","TTL":20,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"198.51.100.45"}]}}]}'
```
ops-bot: Change submitted: CID C998877. Monitoring propagation.
Diego: adding temporary resolver list to our egress: include Google's 8.8.8.8 as a fallback for probes to see if problem is CF-specific.
Rina: updating status page draft: "We are investigating elevated DNS resolution errors impacting some EU users. Mitigation underway." Any wording preferences? keep "intermittent" and "may see 5xx errors".
Tom: applying routing policy switch now to prefer fallback set for eu queries.
Tom: routing change applied. Control-plane reports success. Waiting for probes.
Diego: probe sweep: within ~30s many probes now resolving to eu-central fallback IP, error rate dropping from 22% -> 6% on our probes.
Leah: good. Noting side effect: lower TTL will spike DNS request QPS; Sasha (cost) - FYI, might see egress change.
ops-bot: Alert: DNS QPS for edge egress increased x2.1 since TTL change.
Leah: acknowledged. We'll revert TTL after stability.
Tom: pinging Cloudflare liaison: @cf-liaison could you check for known resolver issues or recent maintenance in eu-west? Please include AS/BGP anomalies if relevant.
cf-liaison: pinged CF support (case #CF-4521). They replied: "No scheduled maintenance, investigating resolver flap on eu-west POPs. Asking for dig logs and timestamps."
Diego: uploading query captures to s3://redwood-incidents/2077771234/dns-captures.tar.gz and shared link with CF.
Leah: customer impact assessment: multi-tenant inference endpoints in EU might have experienced increased error rates and latency for ~6-9 minutes before fallback applied. Enterprise customers IM'd; CS notified.
Rina: opening incident ticket INC-207777 in Jira and assigning for 72h postmortem. I'll own the write-up.
Tom: propose we keep fallback preference for 15 minutes, then gradually revert by reintroducing eu-west primary over 10 minutes once CF confirms resolvers stable.
cf-liaison: CF support: "We've mitigated an internal resolver daemon crash cluster-wide in eu-west-02, propagation in progress. Recommend monitoring for 15m before revert." Quote from CF: incident ref 112233.
Leah: plan: 1) keep fallback for 15m, 2) monitor DNS error rate and application errors 3) if stable, roll TTL up to 60 and remove fallback set. Assignments: Diego - probes/metrics, Tom - routing revert, Rina - incident doc & customer comms.
oncall-rota-bot: Leah (SRE) on-call -> handoff to Tom in 45m unless incident escalates.
Diego: added synth checks hitting multiple EU resolvers every 20s and alert if SERVFAIL > 2% over 2m.
Rina: status page updated via status-bot: "Mitigation in place; DNS provider investigating. Some EU users may experience intermittent errors."
Leah: also adding a short note to ops runbook: if external resolver flap suspected, add external fallback resolver + route53 fallback and reduce TTLs.
Tom: creating a small automation to re-run rollback steps only if CF confirms stability and our error rate <1% for 10 minutes.
Leah: good. I'll stay on until the handoff; will add timeline entries: 2077771234 - alert; 2077771245 - TTL lowered + fallback created; 2077771260 - routing pref applied; 2077771290 - CF confirmed mitigation; 2077771389 - monitoring stable and severity downgraded.
cf-liaison: CF finished: "Resolver cluster recovered; propagation complete." Closing CF ref 112233.
Diego: probes show error rate back down to 0.4% and latency normalized.
Tom: starting gradual revert: increasing TTL back to 60 then removing fallback set after 10m.
ops-bot: auto-adjusting incident severity to P3 - mitigation successful, monitoring.
Rina: incident ticket updated, will schedule postmortem within 72h.
Leah: thanks all. Postmortem owner: Rina. Follow-ups: add automated check for resolver-originated SERVFAIL patterns to alert earlier, and include CF liaison contact in runbook.
status-bot: Status page message: "Issue mitigated; provider recovered. Monitoring continues."
